findings.title: Call to non-existent no-arg isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() — does not compile / wrong overload
findings.body: UsernameForm.authenticate() calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no arguments, but the only method defined (in UsernamePasswordForm, line 160) is `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)`. No no-arg overload exists in UsernamePasswordForm, AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator, or any superclass shown. Either this does not compile, or if an overload exists elsewhere it is being invoked unintentionally. The call must pass the user (e.g. `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())`) so the skip-form shortcut is suppressed exactly when conditional passkeys are active for the re-authenticating user.

findings.title: Conditional passkey UI no longer rendered on the initial login page when no user is set
findings.body: The refactoring moved `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` out of the `else` (user == null) branch and now only calls it when `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())` is true, and that helper (line 160-162) requires `user != null`. On the initial username/password page the user is not yet known, so the WebAuthn challenge/RP-ID/conditional-UI attributes are never set and the passkey autofill (`//form[@id='webauth']`) disappears from the first login page for non-discoverable keys. This regresses the passkeys feature for the common first-visit case and contradicts the test expectations in PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.passwordLoginWithNonDiscoverableKey (line 144-146) and PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest.passwordLoginWithNonDiscoverableKey (lines 189-194), which assert the webauthn form is present on the initial page before any username is submitted. The gate should enable conditional passkeys when passkeys are enabled for the realm, regardless of whether the user is already set.

findings.title: Re-authenticating users without any passkey are now forced through the username form
findings.body: UsernameForm.authenticate() previously auto-succeeded during re-authentication when the user was already set and had no linked brokers. Now, whenever `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` is true (a realm-level passkeys policy flag, not per-user), the form is always shown. A user who has never registered a passkey (and whose administrator merely enabled passkeys for the realm) must re-enter their username on every re-authentication (e.g. prompt=login), even though the user identity is already known. The suppression should also check that the user actually has a passwordless WebAuthn credential, not just the realm policy flag.

findings.title: shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators hook can now be true while user is null
findings.body: fillContextForm previously guarded the WebAuthnAuthenticatorsBean construction on `user != null`; the new `shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators(context)` hook defaults to `context.getUser() != null` in WebAuthnAuthenticator, so behavior is preserved there — but any subclass that returns true without a user (the hook is now an extension point) would pass a null user into `new WebAuthnAuthenticatorsBean(...)` at line 103, risking an NPE. The null-user invariant should be enforced in fillContextForm itself (e.g. `user != null && shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators(context)`), not delegated to every subclass.

findings.title: No test for passkey failure during re-authentication after wrong password (error path keeps username hidden)
findings.body: The new helper AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError and its use in WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.createErrorResponse (the passkey-fails-during-re-auth path, where the username must remain hidden and registration disabled) is not covered: webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthenticationWithPasswordOrPasskey only tests a wrong *password* followed by a successful passkey, never a failing passkey submission during re-authentication. A regression that re-renders the re-auth form with a visible/editable username field would go undetected.
